Subject: Need temporary retention for expanded debug traces (Inc S-8245)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking our call this morning. The engineering team at Acme is still seeing the intermittent deserialization failures and we believe having the full verbose traces (including some payload metadata) captured for an extra 7–14 days will help us reproduce and fix the bug. Right now our remediation depends on you keeping the debug logs beyond the normal 30d purge window for a short, scoped period.

Can Redwood make a short-term exception (we're asking for +14 days) and confirm the residency of the retained logs (we need them to remain within US regions)? Also please confirm how you will handle PII and whether the logs can be masked. I attached a small sample of the error output for your reference.

Attachments: error-sample.log (text, 38KB)

Marissa / Jenna —

Quick security note on our side: Redwood's standard operational policy is 30 days for debug/verbose traces in hosted accounts unless otherwise contractually specified. Exceptions are possible but must be:

- Limited in scope to a named incident (e.g., S-8245)
- Timeboxed with a maximum duration (we typically approve up to 14 days)
- Stored in a specified residency region (you requested US-West; that's acceptable)
- Redacted/masked for PII where applicable, or encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key if sensitive
- Approved in writing by Legal and Security and logged as a retention exception (audit trail required)

Operationally, we'll need:
1) A short justification (one paragraph) signed by the customer point of contact (Jenna).
2) Confirmation of exact start and end timestamps.
3) Whether you'll accept encryption with a Redwood-managed key or need to bring your own key (CMK).

If you can provide those, I can greenlight a scoped policy change. Note that if PII is present, we'll require either redaction or a CMK and documentation that Acme has approved retention for debugging.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Need temporary retention for expanded debug traces (Inc S-8245)

Flagging the engineering plan and caveats. We can implement a short-term retention override scoped to this incident. Proposed approach:

1) Spin up an isolated storage bucket in us-west-2 with a 14-day retention policy (explicitly timeboxed).
2) Ingest only the log categories requested (we should avoid retaining full request payloads unless necessary).
3) Apply a PII-masking script on ingestion (simple regex-based masking for emails/SSNs) and enable server-side encryption. We can optionally use a customer-managed key but that requires KMS onboarding (adds ~24–48 hours).
4) Enable immutable audit logging and attach the INF-2139 infra ticket for the change so we have a revert path.

Impact & ask: this is operationally straightforward but not automatic. I'll need an infra ticket (INF-2139) created and approval to create a non-default retention policy. Also want written confirmation from Acme that they agree to the masking approach and the 14-day window. Cost: negligible for 14 days of logs but note we will surface the storage charge on the next invoice.

If you confirm, I'll kick off the infra changes and coordinate with Neha to ensure audit and key handling are correct.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Logs retained under this exception must be encrypted at rest; Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for the initial window, but if Acme prefers CMK we will support that (note: CMK onboarding may add time).
3) PII must be masked to the extent practicable; if masking cannot remove a category of regulated data, we require a signed acknowledgement from Acme confirming they accept the temporary retention for debugging purposes.
4) Security must enable audit logging and append the exception to the contract record (please add a note to the HubSpot company record): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/ACME

Assuming the above, I authorize Security and Infra to proceed with a one-time, 14-day retention override. Please ensure the exception-form.pdf is completed and stored in our records.
